title: A RNN-Based Mobile Application for Intelligent Personal Budget Management and Financial Trend Prediction
tldr: A mobile-first intelligent budget management application integrating RNN-based financial trend prediction with rule-based advisory, achieving 86.63% directional prediction accuracy and 97.5% user satisfaction through a hybrid architecture combining local processing with cloud-based deep learning.
problem_and_motivation: Traditional budgeting tools provide static record-keeping without predictive capabilities, leaving users to make reactive financial decisions. Existing systems fail to deliver both automated expense tracking and forward-looking insights within a unified mobile interface. There is a gap between simple expense trackers and sophisticated ML platforms in terms of accessibility and integrated predictive intelligence for personal budget management.
approach: Developed a hybrid architecture combining local Android processing with cloud-based RNN prediction services.
Implemented a three-layer model: data layer (Room database, Firebase), logic layer (RNN, rules engine), and interface layer (Material Design).
Trained RNN model on 1,500 anonymized financial records across six expense categories with temporal features.
Implemented rule-based advisory engine triggered by predicted budget status thresholds.
Applied data augmentation for minority financial situations using SMOTE-like oversampling.
Integrated real-time expense tracking with automatic categorization using category heuristics.
Conducted evaluation using directional prediction accuracy, MAE, and user satisfaction surveys.
Achieved 82% computational efficiency through local preprocessing of categorical features before cloud RNN inference.
findings: Hybrid RNN achieves 86.63% directional prediction accuracy and 0.92 correlation coefficient.
97.5% of surveyed users report the application as effective for budget management.
Local preprocessing reduces cloud computation load by 82% while maintaining prediction accuracy.
Combined RNN and rule-based approach outperforms either technique individually.
RNN prediction combined with threshold-based alerts achieves 89.2% accuracy for budget status prediction.
Computational overhead is 40% lower than pure cloud-based prediction architectures.
Real-time feedback mechanism improves financial behavior adherence by 23% compared to passive tools.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This paper contributes a mobile-first intelligent budget management platform that combines RNN-based financial trend prediction with rule-based advisory within a hybrid local-cloud architecture, demonstrating 86.63% directional prediction accuracy and 97.5% user satisfaction. It introduces a practical approach to reducing cloud computation load by 82% through local preprocessing while maintaining prediction quality, and validates that combined RNN-rule approaches outperform either technique individually for personal budget management.
directly_justifies: Hybrid RNN achieves 86.63% directional accuracy for financial trend prediction.
Local preprocessing reduces cloud computation by 82% without sacrificing accuracy.
Combined RNN and rule-based approach outperforms standalone techniques.
97.5% user satisfaction rate demonstrates practical effectiveness.
Real-time feedback improves financial behavior adherence by 23%.
limits: RNN architecture lacks LSTM/GRU gating mechanisms for very long sequences.
Evaluation on limited user base (40 respondents) for satisfaction metrics.
Does not address irregular income patterns or multi-currency scenarios.
Cloud dependency for RNN inference limits full offline functionality.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: The paper was systematically scanned across all 14 topic domains. Domain 6 (Predictive Modeling) received high relevance for RNN-based financial prediction. Domain 7 (Budgeting) received high relevance for budget management and dynamic alerts. Domain 9 (Mobile Design) received high relevance as the core platform is mobile-first. Domain 11 (Recommendations) received high relevance for the rule-based advisory engine. Domains 1-3, 5, 8, 10, 12, 13, and 14 were considered and rejected as the paper does not address Filipino demographics, financial data APIs, expense categorization frameworks, anomaly detection, privacy, or synthetic data generation.
